name: app.R
content:
library(shiny)

# Part 2b: Compare reported arrests across US states (1973).
ui <- navbarPage(
  "US Arrests Explorer",
  tabPanel("State comparison",
    fluidRow(
      column(4,
        selectInput("offense", "Arrest measure:",
                    choices = c("Murder" = "Murder", "Assault" = "Assault", "Rape" = "Rape")),
        sliderInput("minUrban", "Minimum urban population (%):",
                    min = 0, max = 100, value = 0, step = 5),
        numericInput("topN", "Number of states to display:", value = 10, min = 1, max = 50)
      ),
      column(8,
        plotOutput("statePlot", height = "450px"),
        h4("States shown in the chart"),
        tableOutput("stateTable")
      )
    )
  ),
  tabPanel("About",
    h3("About the data"),
    p("The USArrests dataset contains arrest rates for murder, assault, and rape per 100,000 residents, and urban population percentages, for 50 US states in 1973."),
    p("Source: R built-in datasets package, USArrests.")
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # A single reactive selection drives the plot and table.
  selectedStates <- reactive({
    states <- data.frame(State = rownames(USArrests), USArrests,
                         row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE)
    states <- states[states$UrbanPop >= input$minUrban, , drop = FALSE]
    states <- states[order(states[[input$offense]], decreasing = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
    head(states, input$topN)
  })

  output$statePlot <- renderPlot({
    states <- selectedStates()
    validate(need(nrow(states) > 0, "No states match your urban population filter."))
    par(mar = c(5, 10, 5, 2))
    barplot(rev(states[[input$offense]]), names.arg = rev(states$State),
            horiz = TRUE, las = 1, col = "#3E8F88",
            xlab = paste(input$offense, "arrests per 100,000 residents"),
            main = paste("Highest", input$offense, "arrest rates"),
            sub = "Source: R datasets::USArrests (1973)")
  })

  output$stateTable <- renderTable({
    states <- selectedStates()
    data.frame(State = states$State,
               `Arrests per 100,000 residents` = states[[input$offense]],
               `Urban population (%)` = states$UrbanPop,
               check.names = FALSE)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
